routes.title: AlertUp — Indoor Wayfinding & Emergency Routes from a QR Code
routes.description: Scan one QR code to find any shop, office or room inside a building — with step-by-step routes across floors, lifts and escalators. The same codes switch to evacuation routes in an emergency.

content.h1: Find your way inside any building.
content.lead: AlertUp turns a building's floor plans into a map people can search. Owners place walkways, shops and exits, link the escalators and lifts between floors, then print a QR code for every entrance and corridor. A visitor scans one code, types the shop they are looking for, and gets a step-by-step route — including which escalator to take and which floor to get off at. If an emergency is declared, every code in the building switches to evacuation routing instantly.
bullets: Indoor wayfinding — search for a shop, desk or room and follow a route that spans floors automatically.
Emergency evacuation — the same printed codes switch to the nearest safe exit the moment an emergency is declared.
Wayfinder AI — visitors can ask in plain language and get an answer that knows which floor they are standing on.
Accessible routing — step-free routes that avoid stairs and escalators on request.

faq.question: What is AlertUp?
faq.answer: AlertUp is an indoor wayfinding platform. Building owners turn their floor plans into a searchable map — walkways, shops, rooms, exits and the escalators and lifts that link the floors — and print a QR code for every entrance and corridor. A visitor scans a code, searches for where they are going, and follows a step-by-step route. The same codes double as the building's evacuation system: when an emergency is declared they switch to showing the fastest way out.

faq.question: Do I need to install an app?
faq.answer: No. AlertUp runs entirely in your phone's browser. Scanning a code opens that floor's map straight away, with nothing to download and no account required.

faq.question: How does it find a shop on another floor?
faq.answer: When the building is mapped, the escalators, lifts and stairs are linked between floors. If you search for a shop upstairs, AlertUp works out the whole journey: the walk to the right escalator, which floor to get off at, and the walk to the shop. Each leg is shown on its own floor plan, and you confirm when you arrive — or rescan a code on the new floor, which re-anchors the route automatically.

faq.question: Can it avoid stairs and escalators?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask for a step-free route and AlertUp routes through lifts and level walkways instead. If no step-free route exists, it still gives you a route rather than nothing, and tells you plainly that the journey includes stairs or an escalator.

faq.question: What happens during an emergency?
faq.answer: Someone with permission puts the building into emergency mode. Every screen already open updates within moments, and every new scan opens the route to the nearest emergency exit instead of the shop search. If a visitor is already safe they can dismiss the alert and keep browsing, but a warning bar stays on screen until the emergency is resolved.

faq.question: How do I add my building?
faq.answer: Create a free account, add the building and a plan for each floor, then use the map editor to place walkways, mark shops and exits, and link the floors. AlertUp generates a printable QR code for every location. Your first building is free; larger portfolios and enterprise sites are on paid plans.

howTo.name: How to find your way with AlertUp
howTo.description: Scan an AlertUp QR code, search for where you are going, and follow the route across floors.

steps.name: Scan the nearest AlertUp code
steps.text: Codes are printed around the building — at entrances, lifts and junctions. Point your phone camera at one, or open alertup.world/scan and use the built-in scanner. No app needed.

steps.name: Search for where you're going
steps.text: The floor's map opens with your position already marked. Type a shop, room or category — or tap 'nearest exit' if that is what you need.

steps.name: Follow the route across floors
steps.text: Walk the highlighted path. When the route changes floor it tells you which escalator or lift to take and which floor to get off at; confirm when you arrive, or scan a code on the new floor to re-anchor.
